comparison: Perfect agreement on sensorimotor dysfunction claims (C4, C33-C35). Both evaluations find the behavioral evidence for increased startle response and decreased PPI to be well-supported and describe these as solid results.

Perfect agreement on astrogliosis findings (C7, C53, C55). Both evaluations support the GFAP immunohistochemistry results showing widespread inflammation, with peer reviewer describing it as 'striking astrogliosis' and OpenEval noting appropriate statistical methods.

Perfect agreement on HPC-PFC connectivity impairments (C79-C86). Both evaluations support reduced theta coherence and altered cross-correlation findings, with OpenEval emphasizing convergent evidence from multiple analytical approaches and peer reviewer accepting these as solid electrophysiological results.

Perfect agreement on REM-like active states (C10, C87-C90). Both evaluations support the state map analysis and machine learning validation findings, with peer reviewer implicitly accepting this as part of comprehensive electrophysiological assessment.

Perfect agreement on epileptiform activity (C65-C67). Both evaluations support the characterization of state-dependent epileptiform discharges, though OpenEval notes the inference of epileptogenesis is somewhat speculative without longitudinal data.

Perfect agreement on discriminant analysis (C97-C99). Both evaluations support the excellent classification accuracy, with OpenEval emphasizing the robustness of the electrophysiological signature and peer reviewer implicitly accepting these as consistent with solid findings.

Perfect agreement on sleep architecture (C64). Both evaluations support the null finding that gross sleep architecture is preserved, with OpenEval noting this is important for interpreting state-specific oscillatory findings.

Strong agreement on working memory deficits (C3, C29-C30). Both evaluations support these findings as solid results. OpenEval additionally evaluates C31-C32 regarding preserved reference memory and learning curves, which peer reviewer does not explicitly address.

Strong agreement on absence of neuronal loss (C5, C50, C54). Both evaluations support that behavioral impairments occur without obvious cell loss. Peer reviewer also implicitly accepts C51-C52 (negative findings in other regions) as part of comprehensive anatomical assessment (see R6).

Strong agreement on increased theta power (C68, C70-C71). Both evaluations support the finding of increased hippocampal theta power during awake state. OpenEval emphasizes methodological rigor in controlling for movement and aperiodic activity using FOOOF parametrization.

Strong agreement on reduced theta-gamma coupling (C9, C73). Both evaluations support this finding as a solid electrophysiological result. OpenEval additionally evaluates C74-C75, noting the mechanistic link to cognitive deficits is speculative.

Partial agreement on LTP findings. Both support increased hippocampal-PFC LTP (C45, C47), with peer reviewer describing these as robust. OpenEval additionally evaluates normal baseline measures (C44, C46) and peer reviewer also addresses the U-shaped relationship (C6, C62) in this result.

Strong agreement on U-shaped relationship between LTP and cognition (C6, C62). Both evaluations support this finding, with peer reviewer stating 'The LTP findings are robust and provide an important avenue for future study' and OpenEval noting appropriate statistical models though cautioning about correlational nature.

Disagreement on multivariate analyses (C56-C58, C60-C61, C63). OpenEval finds these sophisticated analyses well-supported despite modest sample size. Peer reviewer finds these sections 'less compelling than the rest of the paper' and states they 'take away from the impact of the actual findings.'

Disagreement on PCA analysis (C37-C43). OpenEval supports the PCA showing distinct behavioral dimensions despite modest sample size. Peer reviewer expresses reservations about dimensionality reduction approaches generally, though makes exception for U-shaped LTP-cognition relationship.

Strong agreement on dopamine findings (C8, C91-C93, C95). Both evaluations support apomorphine hypersensitivity and neurochemical changes. Peer reviewer notes 'The rationale for the apomorphine experiments are now explained more fully,' suggesting initial concerns were addressed. OpenEval also evaluates C96 separately (see R16).

Agreement on glutamate/GABA findings (C96). OpenEval explicitly supports this finding suggesting excitation/inhibition imbalance. Peer reviewer implicitly accepts this as part of the neurochemical characterization alongside dopamine findings.

Agreement on negative anatomical findings (C51-C52). OpenEval supports these as part of comprehensive assessment showing behavioral impairments without neuronal loss. Peer reviewer implicitly accepts these null results without questioning their validity.

OpenEval evaluates ELS model validation (C23-C25) with behavioral and electrophysiological confirmation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewer does not question the model validity.

OpenEval evaluates control for confounders showing weight recovery (C26-C28). No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though these controls support that behavioral effects are not due to nutritional differences.
OpenEval rates theta-gamma phase locking (C76-C77) as UNCERTAIN due to marginal statistical significance (p=0.0656). No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific finding.

OpenEval rates reduced PPF interpretation as ceiling effect (C48-C49) as UNCERTAIN, noting alternative mechanisms not ruled out. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific interpretation.
